questions.prompt: What is the difference between minification and compression?

options.text: They are the same thing with different names
Minification removes source cruft at build time; compression shrinks the bytes in transit and is reversed by the browser
Minification encrypts the file; compression signs it
Compression happens at build time; minification happens on the server

questions.explanation: Minification strips whitespace/comments (and shortens JS names) at build time; compression (gzip/Brotli/zstd) reduces the transferred bytes and the browser decompresses them. They're independent and stack.

questions.prompt: The request header in which the browser advertises the compression algorithms it supports is ____.
questions.explanation: The browser sends Accept-Encoding (e.g. gzip, br, zstd); the server replies with Content-Encoding naming the algorithm it actually used.

questions.prompt: Which files should you NOT re-compress because they're already compressed? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: JPEG, WebP/AVIF, and WOFF2 are already compressed — re-compressing wastes CPU for no gain. Text like CSS is highly compressible and should be compressed.

questions.prompt: Which algorithm usually compresses text smaller than gzip?
questions.explanation: Brotli typically produces smaller text than gzip, especially when files are precompressed at a high level. zstd is a newer option with emerging support.

questions.prompt: Match each term to what it is.

pairs.right: Build-time removal of whitespace and comments
Transfer-time byte reduction, reversed by the browser
Server header naming the algorithm it used

questions.explanation: Minification is a build step, compression is a transfer step, and the two encoding headers negotiate which algorithm is used.

questions.prompt: Order how a JavaScript file ends up small on the wire and usable in the browser.

items.text: Minify the source at build time
Precompress it with Brotli at build
Browser requests it, sending Accept-Encoding: br
Browser decompresses to the original code

questions.explanation: Minify then precompress at build; at request time the browser advertises support, the server sends the Brotli version, and the browser decompresses it.
